E2014.title: Use of moved value
E2014.template: '{name}' has been moved and cannot be used again
E2014.help: The value has been moved to a new owner. To use it again, use a reference or clone it.

E2016.title: Immutable assignment
E2016.help: Declare the variable with `mut` to allow assignment.

E2018.title: Mutable/immutable borrow conflict
E2018.help: Ensure no immutable references exist before creating a mutable reference.

E2019.title: Double free
E2019.help: Ensure the value is freed only once.

E2020.title: Use after free
E2020.help: Use the value before it is freed, or refactor the code.

E2027.title: unsafe dereference
E2027.template: Cannot dereference raw pointer outside of an `unsafe` block
E2027.help: Wrap the dereference operation in an `unsafe` block.

E3022.title: Entry main signature mismatch
E3022.template: Entry '{name}' signature mismatch: called with zero arguments at runtime, but it requires '{expected}', found '{found}'
E3022.help: The program entry is always called with no arguments. Write main in the parameterless form `main: () -> Void = { ... }`; for external input, use std.os's argv/environment variables.

E3023.title: Top-level executable statements are not allowed
E3023.message: In Bin role, the program body is main; the top level can only contain declarations
E3023.template: In Bin role (yaoxiang.toml is present), top-level executable statements are not allowed — the program body is main
E3023.help: Move this statement into the main function body; if you really want top-level statements to act as the program body, remove yaoxiang.toml and switch to Script mode (without a manifest, top-level statements execute in the order they are written).

E1103.title: Brackets are not allowed in type position
E1103.message: Type arguments use parentheses; brackets are for value-level indexing
E1103.template: '{name}[...]' is not type syntax — type arguments must use parentheses
E1103.help: Write it as `{name}(...)`. Brackets are **value-level** indexing (`list[0]`); in type position only parentheses are allowed: `List(Int)` rather than `List[Int]`.

E3004.title: Unsupported iterator
E3004.help: Currently only range and list iterators are supported.

E3005.title: IR generation error
E3005.help: This is an internal error; please report this issue.

E3006.title: Unresolved variable
E3006.template: IR generation internal error: variable '{name}' failed to resolve
E3006.help: A variable reference remains unresolved at the IR generation stage, indicating the type checker missed it. This is a compiler internal consistency issue; please report this issue.

E3007.title: Top-level binding initialization must be a constant
E3007.template: The initialization of top-level binding '{name}' must be a compile-time constant expression
E3007.help: Top-level bindings are compile-time constants (accessor functions directly return the folded value); runtime-computed initialization is not supported. Please change the computation to a literal/constant operation, or move it into a function body.

E3014.title: Register overflow
E3014.help: Reduce the number of local variables or simplify expressions.

E3019.title: Top-level binding circular dependency
E3019.template: Top-level binding initialization forms a circular dependency: {cycle}
E3019.help: Break the cycle: change the initialization of one of the bindings so it does not reference other bindings in the cycle, or use a function to defer evaluation.

E3020.title: Missing program entry
E3020.help: Define an entry point: main = { ... }. When the Bin role has no main, all functions are unreachable.

E3021.title: Entry is not a function
E3021.template: Program entry '{name}' must be a function, but it is a value binding
E3021.help: Entry must be callable: write as main = { ... } or main: () -> Void = { ... }; value bindings (such as main: Int = 5) will not be executed.

E4010.title: Constant division by zero
E4010.help: Ensure the divisor in a constant expression is not zero.

E4011.title: Constant overflow
E4011.help: The result of the constant expression is out of the range of the type.

E4012.title: Constant recursion too deep
E4012.template: Constant evaluation exceeded maximum recursion depth {limit}
E4012.help: Simplify the constant expression to reduce recursion.

E4014.title: Constant evaluation failed
E4014.template: Failed to evaluate the constant expression: {reason}
E4014.help: Ensure the expression can be evaluated at compile-time.

E4018.title: Refinement predicate violation
E4018.help: The predicate was falsified — there exists an assignment that makes the constraint false. Please check variable values or relax the constraint.

E4019.title: Type equation does not hold
E4019.message: Type equation was falsified in the proof pipeline
E4019.template: Type equation does not hold: expected {expected}, found {found}
E4019.help: Check the type computation of the components or provide a proof function.

E5006.title: Duplicate import
E5006.template: Duplicate import: '{name}' has already been imported

E5007.title: Module exports
E5007.help: Available exports are listed in the error message

E6006.title: Function not found (runtime)
E6006.help: Make sure the function is defined and spelled correctly

E6007.title: Runtime error
E6007.help: See the error message for details

E0016.title: Expected expression
E0016.help: Provide a valid expression at this position
E0016.error_output:
error[E0016]: Expected expression
 --> example.yx:1:5
  |
1 | x = ;
  |     ^ expected expression after '='

E0018.title: Keyword as name
E0018.message: Keywords cannot be used as variable or expression names
E0018.template: '{keyword}' is a keyword and cannot be used as a name
E0018.help: Use a different identifier instead of the keyword
E0018.error_output:
error[E0018]: keyword used as name
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | if = 1;
  | ^^ 'if' is a keyword

E1092.title: Refinement type argument form is illegal
E1092.message: Refinement type argument cannot be converted to a compile-time constant expression
E1092.template: '{name}' requires compile-time constant arguments, but the given argument cannot be converted
E1092.help: Predicate/proof function arguments must be literals, variables, or single-argument type applications, otherwise refinement constraints cannot be generated
E1092.error_output: error[E1092]: 'IsSmall' requires compile-time constant arguments, but the given argument cannot be converted

E1093.title: Refinement argument count mismatch
E1093.help: The number of arguments must match the predicate declaration, otherwise refinement constraints cannot be generated

E1094.title: Unused compile-time value parameter
E1094.message: Compile-time value parameter is not referenced in the type body
E1094.template: '{param}' is declared as a compile-time value parameter of '{type}', but is not referenced in the type body
E1094.help: Please reference the parameter at type positions (field types, inner Fn parameter types, Assert/Array type arguments), or remove it from the declaration
E1094.example: Foo: (T: Type, N: Int) -> Type = { x: T }
E1094.error_output: error[E1094]: 'N' is declared as a compile-time value parameter of 'Foo', but is not referenced in the type body

E1095.title: Unknown interface
E1095.template: Unknown interface: '{name}' (the name referenced in the type body is not a registered type constructor)
E1095.help: Check the spelling of the name, or first declare the interface with `Iface: (Self: Type) -> Type = {{ ... }}`

E1096.title: Interface parameter count mismatch
E1096.help: Provide arguments according to the number of type parameters declared in the interface

E1097.title: Interface member name conflict
E1097.template: Member '{member}' of type '{type}' conflicts with the interface member (fields and methods share a namespace, §1.2)
E1097.help: Rename the field or the interface member

E1098.title: Interface method not implemented
E1098.template: Type '{type}' does not implement method '{method}' of interface '{interface}'
E1098.help: Declare the method with `Type.method: signature = ...`, or provide a binding in the type body

E1099.title: Interface method signature mismatch
E1099.template: Method '{method}' of type '{type}' does not match the interface signature: expected {expected}, found {found}
E1099.help: Make the implementation signature exactly match the interface member signature (§3 forbids overriding, allows overloading)

E1100.title: Duplicate interface method implementation
E1100.template: Method '{method}' of type '{type}' is implemented multiple times (same-signature override is forbidden, §3)
E1100.help: Remove duplicate implementations, keeping only one

E1101.title: Type does not implement interface
E1101.template: Type '{type}' does not implement interface '{interface}' and cannot be used in this existential type position
E1101.help: Implement all members of the interface and instantiate them within the type body (e.g., `Animal(Dog)`); for RFC-011b scenarios (equality/operators), implement the corresponding interface for the type, and linear token fields must be removed first

E1102.title: Loop control statement outside loop
E1102.message: break/continue can only be used inside while/for loop bodies
E1102.help: Move '{keyword}' into the body of a while/for loop

E1064.title: Invalid binding position index
E1064.template: Invalid binding position index: {positions} (function has {total} parameters in total)
E1064.help: Binding positions must fall within the parameter range of the bound function (out of bounds or still negative after normalization). Please check the position numbers of method bindings.

E4020.title: Proof function required
E4020.message: Constraint cannot be proven at compile-time, a proof function is required
E4020.template: A proof function is required to verify the constraint
E4020.help: Add a proof function or provide a runtime check

E4021.title: Loop termination cannot be proven automatically
E4021.message: The compiler cannot synthesize a decreasing measure for this loop, so termination cannot be proven automatically
E4021.template: Cannot prove loop termination automatically: no valid decreasing measure was found
E4021.help: This is a limit of the compiler's automatic reasoning, not a program error. Use a loop form with an explicit decreasing variable (e.g. a counter with a lower bound decremented each iteration), or see RFC-027 §7 for the measure strategies and their coverage.

W1080.title: Compile-time proof degradation
W1080.message: Constraint cannot be proven at compile-time, has been downgraded to runtime check
W1080.template: Constraint cannot be proven at compile-time, has been downgraded to runtime check
W1080.help: Consider adding a proof function to improve safety

E6009.title: Invalid Range step
E6009.help: iter/contains requires a non-zero dynamic step; please check the step expression

E6010.title: Integer parsing failed
E6010.message: String cannot be parsed as an integer
E6010.help: Check whether the string is a valid integer (may contain a sign)

E6011.title: Floating-point parsing failed
E6011.message: String cannot be parsed as a floating-point number
E6011.help: Check whether the string is a valid floating-point number

E2029.title: Reference cycle within spawn
E2029.message: Reference cycle detected within spawn block
E2029.help: References captured by spawn must not form cyclic dependencies; please check the capture list

E3008.title: Unsupported match pattern
E3008.template: match pattern '{pattern}' is not yet implemented: currently only literal and wildcard (_) patterns are supported
E3008.help: Variant destructuring (ok(v)/err(e)/some(x)), structs, tuples, or-patterns, and guards are not yet implemented (planned in RFC-010b). The previous implementation would silently miscompile; this is now rejected at compile-time. Use the `?` operator to handle Result.

E3018.title: Monomorphization instantiation failed
E3018.help: The monomorphizer was unable to generate a specialized version for the given type arguments (common cause: the number of type arguments does not match the generic parameters). Previously this error was silently skipped, only surfacing as a 'function table missing' error at runtime.

E2030.title: Refinement type constraint violated
E2030.template: After assigning '{assigned}', '{var}' no longer satisfies the refinement type constraint: {constraint} (counterexample: {counterexample})
E2030.help: Refinement type annotations require that dependent variables continue to satisfy the predicate constraint after relevant assignments. Adjust the assignment so the constraint holds, or relax the type annotation.

E1014.title: Unknown named argument
E1014.message: The argument name used in the call is not in the function's parameter list
E1014.help: Use one of the names listed in the parameter list, or pass arguments positionally
E1014.error_output:
error[E1014]: Unknown named argument
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | add(b = 1, c = 2);
  |     ^ Function 'add' has no parameter named 'c' (available: a, b)

E1015.title: Argument specified more than once
E1015.message: The same parameter was specified by both a positional and a named argument
E1015.template: Parameter '{name}' of function '{func}' is specified more than once
E1015.help: Each parameter can only be passed once: remove the extra named or positional argument
E1015.error_output:
error[E1015]: Argument specified more than once
 --> example.yx:1:1
  |
1 | add(1, a = 2);
  |          ^ Parameter 'a' of function 'add' is specified more than once

E1104.title: Interface implementation is not in the type's defining module
E1104.message: Operator interface implementations must be written in the type's defining module
E1104.template: Type '{type}' is not defined in this module; interface '{interface}' cannot be implemented for it in this module
E1104.help: Orphan rule: implementations follow the type's defining module. Interface instantiations can only be written for types defined in this module (e.g., `Add(Point, Point, Point)`); operator interfaces for builtin types (Int/List, etc.) are provided by the core and cannot be supplemented

E1105.title: variant constructor cannot be accessed as a field
E1105.message: a variant constructor can only be used in the call form `Type.variant(...)`
E1105.template: '{variant}' is a variant constructor of the enum type '{type}', not a data field
E1105.help: To construct a value, write `{type}.{variant}(...)`; to extract the payload from an enum type value, use match with variant destructuring (RFC-010b). All record-style fields of an enum type have been promoted to variants; runtime values do not carry a field table.
